subject: AWS Marketplace staged credits, term-length tradeoffs, and buyer approver roster (AcmeCorp)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acmecorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Initial proposal: staged credits + term options for AcmeCorp private offer

Hi John / Acme procurement team,

Great talking earlier — appreciate the candid runway constraints for Q1. Per our call, I wanted to put a concise proposal in writing so your procurement and finance teams have a clear starting point. High-level: we can structure an AWS Marketplace private offer that (a) mixes an annual term with usage-based credits for the first 6 months, and (b) phases activation across two BU accounts to reduce up-front cash impact.

Proposal snapshot (optional draft attached):
- Term: 12-month private offer with a 6-month staged credit schedule.
- Staged credits: 40% credit month 1-3, 20% credit month 4-6, then full billing thereafter. Credits apply only to hosted inference usage.
- Buyer approvals: single PO per BU; we’ll need a primary approver and a backup approver listed for finance in the activation doc.
- Evidence: we’ll provide an evidence pack for your security review (SOC2 summary, network diagram, data handling note).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Can procurement confirm the names and emails of the buyer approvers we should route the DocuSign to?
2) Is Acme comfortable with a 12-month term with the credit ramp described, or do you prefer a 6- or 24-month option to trade price vs term?
3) If procurement wants, I can set up a 30-minute call with Neha (finance) and Vanessa (marketplace operations) to walk the activation flow.

I attached a draft private-offer doc and a pricing model so you can see the net effective rates with credits applied.

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: acme-mop-draft.docx (draft private offer), pricing-model-v2.xlsx (workbook)
From: John Lee <john.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: staged credits + term options for AcmeCorp private offer

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the clear options. Procurement reviewed the draft and we have three quick asks before we can escalate to finance:

1) Approver roster: please list the specific set of approver roles we need to route to (e.g., BU procurement approver, BU finance approver, central contract admin). We need the recipient names and emails for routing.
2) Evidence pack: procurement needs the SOC2 certificate, network diagram (redacted ok), and a short SL doc showing latency SLOs per region. We can accept a bundle link or PDFs.
3) Credits mechanics: confirm whether credits can be applied at invoice-line level (so our internal chargeback works) and whether they reduce overage charges or apply only to committed units.

We like the staged approach — keeps cost predictability while easing adoption. Tentatively lean to a 12-month with the 6-month credit ramp, but finance may ask for a 24-month to lower effective rate.

For approvers: I’ll confirm specific people once procurement finalizes the approver list later today.

Would appreciate if your team can send the evidence pack and a note on credit mechanics by EOD.

Regards,

John Lee
Head of Procurement
AcmeCorp

John —

Looping in Vanessa (marketplace ops) to cover activation routing. Quick answers to procurement’s questions:

- Approver roster/roles: we typically route DocuSign in this order: 1) BU Procurement Approver, 2) BU Finance Approver (for chargeback signoff), 3) Central Contract Admin (for legal countersign). If Acme wants an alternate workflow (e.g., procurement-only then finance after activation), we can support that but need it documented before activation.

- Evidence pack: attached here as a single ZIP (evidence-pack-aws-security.pdf is a placeholder filename in the attachments list on my side). The package includes our SOC 2 summary, redacted infra diagram, and a one-pager on SLOs and data handling. If you need full reports we can arrange an NDA/certified transfer.

- Credit mechanics: credits are applied at invoice-line level and can reduce overage lines; for committed units credits first offset committed usage, then apply to overage. We can also model credits as a separate invoice credit line if your accounting prefers. See attached pricing-model-v2.xlsx for examples.

One operational note: for multi-BU activation we recommend provisioning two linked private-offer entitlements (one per BU) so billing stays separated for your chargeback. That does add a small operational step during activation but avoids post-facto invoicing splits.

Vanessa — can you confirm the typical DocuSign TTL (how long the link remains valid) we should set and whether we should pre-populate the region/usage caps in the private-offer?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference
